summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, and a history of left below-knee amputation was admitted for severe right foot pain and dry gangrene. Imaging revealed subcutaneous emphysema, indicating tissue necrosis. She was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, and after a urine culture identified Pseudomonas aeruginosa sensitive to ciprofloxacin, targeted therapy was continued. Due to extensive gangrene, she underwent a right below-knee amputation. Postoperatively, pain was initially difficult to control but improved with transition to oral morphine. Psychiatric consultation was obtained after she expressed suicidal thoughts, and citalopram was initiated for mood support. Her recovery progressed well, with stable vital signs, improving lab values, and good wound healing. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with a plan for ongoing antibiotic therapy, diabetes management, and multidisciplinary follow-up.
